versions.content: White list definition for DID s The white list for DID s defines the set of data identifiers that are allowed to be read, written and controlled. Each entry shall contain in the first two bytes the DID number and in the third byte the following access definitions: • Bit 0: Read access • Bit1: Write access • Bit2: Control access (by InputOutputControlByIdentifier) A bit value of 0 means that the operation is forbidden, a bit value of 1 means that the operation is allowed. All not used bits (3-7) shall be set to zero. DID numbers are always in big endian format (MSB first).
